q1: SELECT b.name AS bar, COUNT(DISTINCT f.drinker) AS num_drinker, AVG(s.price) AS avg_price, (SELECT f1.drinker FROM frequents AS f1 WHERE f1.bar = b.name ORDER BY f1.times_a_week DESC, f1.drinker ASC LIMIT 1) AS most_reg_drinker FROM bar AS b LEFT JOIN frequents AS f ON b.name = f.bar LEFT JOIN serves AS s ON b.name = s.bar GROUP BY b.name ORDER BY num_drinker DESC, b.name ASC
q2: SELECT bar, total_num_drinker, avg_price, most_reg_drinker FROM (SELECT DISTINCT name AS bar FROM BAR ORDER BY name) AS barname NATURAL JOIN (SELECT COUNT(drinker) AS total_num_drinker, bar FROM frequents GROUP BY bar ORDER BY total_num_drinker DESC) AS drinkercount NATURAL JOIN (SELECT AVG(price) AS avg_price, bar FROM serves GROUP BY bar) AS avgprices NATURAL JOIN (SELECT MAX(drinker) AS most_reg_drinker, bar FROM frequents JOIN (SELECT MAX(times_a_week) AS mostreg, bar AS bar2 FROM frequents GROUP BY bar) AS maxbarlist ON times_a_week = mostreg AND bar = bar2 GROUP BY bar) AS regdrinkers ORDER BY total_num_drinker DESC

The ordering is by num_drinker descending and bar name ascending.

Then it joins with drinkercount which is COUNT(drinker) per bar, grouped by bar, ordered by total_num_drinker descending. Then avgprices is AVG(price) per bar from Serves, grouped by bar. Then regdrinkers is a subquery that finds the most regular drinker. The inner part of regdrinkers is a maxbarlist that gets the max times_a_week per bar. Then joining that with Frequents on times_a_week equals mostreg and bar equals bar2, grouping by bar, and selecting MAX(drinker) as most_reg_drinker.

So the key differences I see are:

In Q1, the most_reg_drinker is determined by ordering by times_a_week DESC and drinker ASC, then taking the first one. In Q2, the most_reg_drinker is determined by first finding the max times_a_week per bar, then joining back to Frequents to get the drinker(s) with that max times_a_week, and then taking MAX(drinker) (which would be the lexicographically last drinker if multiple have same max times_a_week).

Wait, in Q1's subquery, the order by is times_a_week DESC, drinker ASC. So for ties in times_a_week, the drinker with the smallest name comes first. So the first one in that ordering is the one with the highest times_a_week, and if there's a tie, the one with the smallest drinker name.

In Q2, the approach is: find the max times_a_week per bar (maxbarlist), then join Frequents on that times_a_week and bar to get all drinkers with that max times_a_week, then take MAX(drinker). So if there are multiple drinkers with the same max times_a_week, MAX(drinker) would pick the lexicographically largest one. So this could differ from Q1's approach in case of ties.

For example, suppose two drinkers, Alice and Bob, both have the same max times_a_week. In Q1, ordering by drinker ASC would put Alice first. In Q2, MAX(drinker) would give Bob. So the most_reg_drinker would differ in that case.

So num_drinker in Q1 is equivalent to total_num_drinker in Q2.

For avg_price: Q1 uses AVG(s.price) from Serves joined on bar. Since Serves has one row per bar and beer, grouping by bar gives the average of all prices for that bar. Similarly, Q2's avgprices subquery is AVG(price) grouped by bar, same result. So avg_price is same.
